 -5-  NC: 2023:KHC:28962  MFA No. 8156 of 2017  C/W MFA No. 6290 of 2018  JUDGMENT 1. MFA 8156/2017 is filed by the Insurance Company and MFA 6290/2018 is filed by the claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short)

being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 26.7.2017 passed by the MACT, Mangaluru, D.K.
in MVC 1458/2013.
2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeals briefly stated are that on 22.5.2013 at about 3:20 p.m.,
while the deceased Taranath was walking on the side of Bengaluru- Mangaluru NH-75 at Adyar, at that time, a Tanker bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-5171 which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the deceased.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the NC: 2023:KHC:28962 deceased along with interest.
On service of summons, the respondents appeared through counsel and filed written statements in which the averments made in the petition were denied.

sentences.text: On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimants, in order to prove their case, examined claimant No.1 as PW-1 and examined three more witnesses as PWs-2 to 4 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P13.
On behalf of respondents, three witnesses were examined as RWs-1 to 3 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.R1 to Ex.R6.

The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.12,58,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. NC: 2023:KHC:28962 and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, these appeals have been filed.
5. The learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following contentions:
Regarding Negligence The accident occurred due to negligence of the deceased himself.

The deceased tried to cross the road negligently without following the traffic rules and when he came in the middle of the road, inspite of best efforts, the driver of the tanker could not stop the vehicle and dashed to the deceased.
Therefore, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the tanker.
He further contended that the as per mahazar and inquest report, it is clear that the deceased was crossing the road and accident occurred in the middle of the road.
The Tribunal is not justified in holding that the driver of the tanker alone was negligent in causing the accident.
This finding of the Tribunal is contrary to the materials available on record.
NC: 2023:KHC:28962 Regarding Liability
The offending vehicle was carrying hazardous substance/goods and the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
The insured has violated the policy conditions.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable to indemnify the insured.
The Tribunal has erred in holding that the offending vehicle was not carrying any hazardous goods.

Even though the owner of the offending vehicle appeared before the Tribunal and filed written statement, he has not contended that the offending vehicle was empty and it was not carrying any hazardous goods.
The burden lies on the owner to plead and prove that offending vehicle was not carrying any hazardous substance.
In support of his contention, he has relied upon the decision of this Court in the case of Smt.Uma Raghu -v- Smt.

Mamtaz reported in (2019) ILR (KANT) 508 and in the case of Girish M. -v- Regional Manager, New India Assurance Co. Ltd.,
Bengaluru reported in AIR ONLINE 2020 KAR 1915.

Regarding Negligence The deceased was walking on the left side of the road cautiously.
The accident occurred on the service road.
The offending vehicle was moving from Mangaluru side in a high speed and rash and negligent manner to the extreme side of the road to the service road and dashed to the deceased.
Due to the impact, he fell down and sustained injuries and succumbed to injuries.
Immediately after the accident, complaint has been lodged.
The police have registered FIR against the driver of the tanker and after investigation have filed charge sheet against the driver of the tanker.
Even as per the sketch and mahazar, it is clear that the driver of the tanker was negligent in causing the accident.
The Tribunal has rightly held that the driver of the tanker alone was negligent in causing the accident.

Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal and original records.
NEGLIGENCE 9.

It is the specific case of the claimants that on 22.5.2013 at about 3:20 p.m., while the deceased Taranath was walking on the side of Bengaluru-Mangaluru NH-75 at Adyar, at that time, a Tanker bearing - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:28962 registration NoKA-01-AB-5171 which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the deceased.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on 23.5.2013.
Hence, the claimants filed claim petition seeking compensation.

To prove the case, the claimants have examined claimant No.1 as PW-1 and two witnesses to the accident as PWs-3 and 4 produced 13 documents.
10.
Under the Motor Vehicles Act in the claim petition before the Claims Tribunal, the standard of proof is much below than what is required in a criminal case as well as in the civil case.

No doubt,
before the Tribunal, there must be some material on the basis of which the Tribunal can arrive or decide things necessary to decide for awarding compensation, but the Tribunal is not expected to take or to adopt a nicety of a civil or criminal case.
After all it is a summary enquiry and it is the legislation for the welfare of the Society.
The proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to the proceedings under civil rules.

Hence,

In the case of MANGLA RAM -v- ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED (2018) 5 SCC 656, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as hereinbelow:
"25.

sentences.text: In Dulcina Fernandes, this Court examined similar situation where the evidence of claimant's eyewitness was discarded by the Tribunal and that the respondent in that case was acquitted in the criminal case concerning the accident.

This Court,
however, opined that it cannot be overlooked that upon investigation of the case registered against the respondent, prima facie, materials showing negligence were found to put him on trial.

The Court restated the settled principle that the evidence of the claimants ought to be examined by the Tribunal on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and certainly the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
11.
In the case on hand, PWs-3 and 4 have categorically stated that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.

In - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:28962 fact, they have categorically stated that the deceased was walking on the left side of the road and the driver of the tanker came in rash and negligent mannder and dashed against the deceased.

As per Ex.P-5-Mahazar and Ex.P-6- sketch, it is clear that deceased was walking on the left side of the service road and driver of the tanker came in a high speed and extreme left side of the service road and dashed to the deceased.
Immediately, complaint was lodged.
The police have registered FIR against the driver of the tanker and after investigation have filed charge sheet against the driver of the tanker.
Therefore, it is very clear from the evidence of the parties and materials available on record that the driver of the tanker was alone negligent in causing the accident.
The Tribunal is justified in answering issue No.1 in the affirmative.
QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION 12.
The claimants claim that deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by working as carpenter at - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:28962 Raghavendra Furniture Works and examined the employer as PW-2.
But they have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
In the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal considering the age and avocation of the deceased has rightly assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- p.m.
To the aforesaid income, 25% has to be added on account of future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in 'PRANAY SETHI' (supra).
Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.11,250/-.

The Insurance Company has taken a specific plea that the offending vehicle was carrying hazardous goods in the tanker and that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
Even the owner of the offending vehicle has appeared and filed written statement before the Tribunal and contended that the tanker was empty and it was not carrying any hazardous goods.

This Court in similar circumstances in the case of Smt.Uma Raghu -v- Smt.Mamtaz reported in (2019) ILR (KANT) 508 in paragraph-16 and 17 has held as follows:
16.

sentences.text: Admittedly, in the fact matrix of these appeals, nothing is coming forth either from the - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC:28962 pleadings or from the evidentiary material as to whether the offending tanker lorry was an empty vehicle or a loaded vehicle at the time of accident.

However, in the absence of plea and evidence, with regard to this, the MACT has fastened the liability only on the insured leaving the insurer to go free, although the reasoning part that led to the operative portion of the order is not articulately worded.
The MACT accepted the contention of the insured that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a special licence and thereby absolved the insurer from the liability.
This is on the assumption that such a special licence was required.
17. In the appeals in hand, as already stated above, there is neither a plea not evidence as to whether the offending vehicle was carrying the hazardous substance when it met with accident.
In the absence of such a plea and evidence, there can be no presumption that the said vehicle was carrying or not carrying the substance.
Thus the due adjudication is not possible for adjudging the issue of liability of the insurer.
Not adjudging the same, may - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC:28962 result into prejudice to the insured or the insurer.

17. Further, this Court in the case of Girish M. -v- Regional Manager, New India Assurance Co. Ltd.,
Bengaluru reported in AIR ONLINE 2020 KAR 1915 in paragraph-9 has held as follows:
9. The Tribunal has recorded a finding that the driver of the tanker lorry did not have a license to drive a transport vehicle with hazardous goods and therefore, the Insurance Company could not be saddled with any liability.

ORDER a) The appeals are allowed in part.

opennyai_summary.facts:
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
The Tribunal further held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.12,58,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. NC: 2023:KHC:28962 and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
The insured has violated the policy conditions.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable to indemnify the insured.
The Tribunal has erred in holding that the offending vehicle was not carrying any hazardous goods.
In the absence of proof of income, the monthly income assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.9,000/- is on the higher side.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The offending vehicle was carrying hazardous substance/goods and the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
Even though the owner of the offending vehicle appeared before the Tribunal and filed written statement, he has not contended that the offending vehicle was empty and it was not carrying any hazardous goods.
Secondly, since the claimants have not established the income of the deceased,
they are not entitled for compensation towards 'future prospects'.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
c) Thirdly, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS [AIR 2017 SC 5157], the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the heads loss of love and affection, loss of estate, loss of consortium and transportation of dead body are on the higher side.
b) Secondly, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS [AIR 2017 SC 5157], in case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 25% of the established income towards 'future prospects' should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on 23.5.2013.
Hence, the claimants filed claim petition seeking compensation.
Under the Motor Vehicles Act in the claim petition before the Claims Tribunal, the standard of proof is much below than what is required in a criminal case as well as in the civil case.
No doubt,
before the Tribunal, there must be some material on the basis of which the Tribunal can arrive or decide things necessary to decide for awarding compensation, but the Tribunal is not expected to take or to adopt a nicety of a civil or criminal case.
After all it is a summary enquiry and it is the legislation for the welfare of the Society.
The proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to the proceedings under civil rules.
In the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal considering the age and avocation of the deceased has rightly assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- p.m.
Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.11,250/-.

In addition, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'loss of estate' and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.
In view of the above judgments cited above and in the facts and circumstances of the case, this court is of the opinion that the matter requires to be remanded to the Tribunal for reconsideration only in respect of liability is concerned, after giving opportunities to both the parties to adduce additional evidence and produce additional documents.

In the result, I pass the following order:
ORDER a) The appeals are allowed in part.
b) The judgment and award of the Tribunal in respect of negligence is concerned, the same is confirmed and in respect of quantum of compensation is concerned, the same is modified.
c) The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.16,47,500/- as against Rs.12,58,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
d) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
e) The apportionment, deposit and release of amount shall be made in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
- 22 - NC: 2023:KHC:28962 f) In view of the order dated 2.12.2020 passed by this Court, the claimants are not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 279 days in filing the appeal.
g) The amount in deposit before this Court is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
h) The judgment and award of the Tribunal in respect of liability is concerned, the same is set aside.
i) The matter is remanded to the Tribunal for reconsideration in respect of liability is concerned.
j) The parties are at liberty to adduce additional evidence and produce additional documents to establish their case.
k) Since the accident is of the year 2013 and in the interest of justice, parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 26.09.2023 without awaiting for any notice from the Tribunal.
l) The Tribunal after giving opportunities to the parties shall decide the matter in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible.
- 23 - NC: 2023:KHC:28962 m)
In case, the Insurance Company succeeds before the Tribunal, it is at liberty to recover the compensation amount from the owner of the offending vehicle.
n)
If the claimants file application for withdrawal of amount, the Tribunal is directed to consider the same.
o) All the contentions of the parties are kept open.
p) Registry is directed to return the records to the Tribunal forthwith.
